headline: Norway scrapped Malaysia's missile deal. The RM6 billion LCS scandal it buries is bigger.
context: Norway revoked the Naval Strike Missile export permit before a March 2026 delivery, after Malaysia paid nearly 95% of the €124m contract. The wider 15-year LCS programme has paid RM6.083 billion to Boustead Naval Shipyard for zero hulls delivered.

changes.summary: Correction: this card said Australia signed its missile deal with Norway on the day Malaysia's dispute went public; the dispute was reported from 6 May, and 14 May was the day Anwar protested to Norway's prime minister.

Correction: we now say the first ship had made its first voyage in January rather than begun sea trials, tie Norway's revocation to the missiles' March 2026 delivery date, give the payment as nearly 95% and quote the Prime Minister's own words, no longer say Malaysia has sued, and removed claims about India, Indonesia and the Government Procurement Act that we could not confirm.

cards.big: Anwar told Norway contracts are 'not confetti.' The first ship the missiles were meant for still awaits delivery.
cards.sub: Norway pulled the approvals before the March 2026 delivery. LCS-1 first sailed in January; handover is due in December. Malaysia paid over RM500m, nearly 95% of the €124m contract.

cards.big: Zero LCS hulls after 15 years and RM6.083b paid to Boustead Naval Shipyard. Zero criminal convictions.
cards.sub: Advance payments up to RM1.36b vs a RM10m Treasury threshold; RM400m settled old NGPV debts. The sole prosecution (RM21.08m CBT, ex-BNS MD Ahmad Ramli) ended in dementia discharge March 2025.

cards.big: Norway invoked force majeure. Its own export rules let it revoke arms-export licences when circumstances change.
cards.sub: MINDEF confirmed force majeure. The contract isn't public, so 'no breach' can't be cleanly drawn. Any suit faces state immunity, governing-law limits, and force-majeure wording.

cards.big: Under US ITAR rules, one US-origin part can pull a whole missile under US re-export jurisdiction. Oslo may not have had a choice.
cards.sub: USNI cited an industry source linking the revocation to a US gyroscope in the NSM's guidance. The ITAR mechanism (22 CFR 120-130) is real; the link is unconfirmed.

cards.big: On 14 May, the day Anwar protested to Norway's prime minister, Australia signed an MoU with Norway to make NSM and JSM missiles locally.
cards.sub: Oslo reserves some of its most sensitive defence technology for 'allies and closest partners'. Norway (2024) and Australia (Sept 2025) recognise Palestine.

cards.big: The scandal isn't Norway revoking a licence. It's using Oslo to bury 15 years of LCS billions: ships undelivered, one DNAA the only criminal endpoint across four governments.
Like paying 95% upfront for a fitting tailored to a suit not yet stitched, then weighing a lawsuit against the tailor when his country bans the fabric.
cards.sub: LCS-1 had first sailed but was not yet handed over when Norway pulled the approvals before the March 2026 delivery. Handover is due in December.

cards.big: Norway acted within its rules. The real cost is 15 years of LCS spending: no delivered ships, one DNAA as the only criminal endpoint across four governments.
